## Claims
- [proved] Assuming the accepted graded basis \(Q=\bigoplus_{\rho\subseteq b^2}\mathbb Z e_\rho\) with \(\deg e_\rho=ij+|\rho|\), for \(b\ge1\) and \(0\le N\le2b\),
\[
\operatorname{rank}Q_{ij+N}=
\begin{cases}
\lfloor N/2\rfloor+1,&0\le N\le b,\\
\lfloor(2b-N)/2\rfloor+1,&b\le N\le2b.
\end{cases}
\]
- [proved] Under the same accepted-basis hypothesis, every \(Q_{ij+N}\) is torsion-free (indeed free abelian), and \(Q_{ij+N}=0\) for \(N\notin[0,2b]\).

## Strategy
Write \(\rho=(x,y)\) with \(b\ge x\ge y\ge0\) and \(x+y=N\).

For \(0\le N\le b\), \(y=0,\ldots,\lfloor N/2\rfloor\), giving \(\lfloor N/2\rfloor+1\) partitions.

For \(b\le N\le2b\), the conditions become
\[
N-b\le y\le\lfloor N/2\rfloor.
\]
Their number is
\[
\lfloor N/2\rfloor-(N-b)+1
=\left\lfloor\frac{2b-N}{2}\right\rfloor+1.
\]
The accepted basis identifies these counts with the indicated graded ranks. Since each graded piece has a subset of this integral basis, it is free abelian.

The requested target is established, conditional only on the accepted graded-basis statement.
